segments.he: ״אַל יַכְּךָ״, וִ״יבָרֶכְךָ״, וְ״יֵיטִיב לָךְ״ – רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if one says to the witnesses: God «shall not strike you, or:» God «shall bless you, or:» God «shall benefit you» if you come and testify, «Rabbi Meir deems» him «liable,» as one may infer from that statement that if he fails to testify God will strike him, or will not bless or benefit him. «And the Rabbis deem» him «exempt» because the curse is not explicitly stated.

positions.claim: an oath of testimony by a blessing formula implying a curse makes the witness liable
positions.basis: the curse is inferred from the blessing

positions.claim: the witness is exempt since the curse is not explicit
